books.name: The Stargazing Society
books.focus: No sooner · albeit · let alone · whatsoever · Much as

items.s: ___ sooner had the club's new telescope arrived than everyone wanted a turn.
items.tip: No sooner had … than = the second thing happened immediately after the first.
items.say: No sooner had the club's new telescope arrived than everyone wanted a turn.
items.ask: Blank sooner had the club's new telescope arrived than everyone wanted a turn.

items.s: Setting it up, ___ time-consuming, proved well worth the effort.
items.tip: albeit = although (followed by an adjective or phrase, not a full clause).
items.say: Setting it up, albeit time-consuming, proved well worth the effort.
items.ask: Setting it up, blank time-consuming, proved well worth the effort.

items.s: Few of us had ever seen Saturn's rings, ___ alone its moons.
items.tip: let alone = and even less (its moons are even harder to see).
items.say: Few of us had ever seen Saturn's rings, let alone its moons.
items.ask: Few of us had ever seen Saturn's rings, blank alone its moons.

items.s: On the first clear night, there was no cloud ___.
items.tip: no + noun + whatsoever = none at all (very strong).
items.say: On the first clear night, there was no cloud whatsoever.
items.ask: On the first clear night, there was no cloud blank.

items.s: ___ as we wanted to stay out until dawn, we had school at eight.
items.tip: Much as = although (we really wanted to).
items.say: Much as we wanted to stay out until dawn, we had school at eight.
items.ask: Blank as we wanted to stay out until dawn, we had school at eight.

items.s: Not ___ did anyone complain about the cold.
items.tip: Not once + question order = never, not a single time.
items.say: Not once did anyone complain about the cold.
items.ask: Not blank did anyone complain about the cold.

items.s: Our teacher insisted that the telescope ___ packed away by eleven.
items.tip: insist that + subject + be (the formal subjunctive). 'was' is also heard in British English.
items.say: Our teacher insisted that the telescope be packed away by eleven.
items.ask: Our teacher insisted that the telescope blank packed away by eleven.

items.s: The society has since grown ___ over forty members.
items.tip: grow to + a number = reach that number.
items.say: The society has since grown to over forty members.
items.ask: The society has since grown blank over forty members.

books.name: The Castle Ruins
books.focus: all that · legend has it · lest · Should · insofar as

items.s: Perched on a cliff, the ruined tower is all ___ remains of a once-mighty fortress.
items.tip: all that remains = the only thing left (after all, use that, not which).
items.say: Perched on a cliff, the ruined tower is all that remains of a once-mighty fortress.
items.ask: Perched on a cliff, the ruined tower is all blank remains of a once-mighty fortress.

items.s: Little is known about ___ built it, though stories abound.
items.tip: about who built it: who is the subject of 'built'.
items.say: Little is known about who built it, though stories abound.
items.ask: Little is known about blank built it, though stories abound.

items.s: Local legend has ___ that a dragon once guarded the gates.
items.tip: Legend has it that… = people say (in old stories) that…
items.say: Local legend has it that a dragon once guarded the gates.
items.ask: Local legend has blank that a dragon once guarded the gates.

items.s: We were told to keep to the path ___ we slip on the crumbling stones.
items.tip: lest = so that … not (very formal): lest we slip = so that we don't slip.
items.say: We were told to keep to the path lest we slip on the crumbling stones.
items.ask: We were told to keep to the path blank we slip on the crumbling stones.

items.s: ___ the walls collapse, centuries of history would be lost.
items.tip: Should + subject + verb = If (by any chance) the walls collapse… a formal inverted conditional (like Were the walls to collapse).
items.say: Should the walls collapse, centuries of history would be lost.
items.ask: Blank the walls collapse, centuries of history would be lost.

items.s: Volunteers, ___ of whom are paid, spend their weekends repairing it.
items.tip: none of whom = not one of them (they work for free).
items.say: Volunteers, none of whom are paid, spend their weekends repairing it.
items.ask: Volunteers, blank of whom are paid, spend their weekends repairing it.

items.s: Their efforts have paid ___, as the castle now welcomes thousands of visitors a year.
items.tip: pay off = bring good results after hard work.
items.say: Their efforts have paid off, as the castle now welcomes thousands of visitors a year.
items.ask: Their efforts have paid blank, as the castle now welcomes thousands of visitors a year.

items.s: ___ as it is possible, the repairs are done using traditional methods.
items.tip: Insofar as = to the extent that (as much as it can be).
items.say: Insofar as it is possible, the repairs are done using traditional methods.
items.ask: Blank as it is possible, the repairs are done using traditional methods.

books.name: The Youth Orchestra
books.focus: to say the least · be it · Hardly · on the verge of · as though

items.s: Joining the city youth orchestra was, ___ say the least, a challenge.
items.tip: to say the least = and that's putting it mildly (it was harder than that!).
items.say: Joining the city youth orchestra was, to say the least, a challenge.
items.ask: Joining the city youth orchestra was, blank say the least, a challenge.

items.s: The conductor demanded perfection, ___ it at rehearsals or on stage.
items.tip: be it A or B = whether it is A or B.
items.say: The conductor demanded perfection, be it at rehearsals or on stage.
items.ask: The conductor demanded perfection, blank it at rehearsals or on stage.

items.s: ___ a week went by without extra practice.
items.tip: Hardly a week = almost no week (nearly every week had extra practice).
items.say: Hardly a week went by without extra practice.
items.ask: Blank a week went by without extra practice.

items.s: There were moments when I was on the ___ of giving up.
items.tip: on the verge of + -ing = very close to doing it.
items.say: There were moments when I was on the verge of giving up.
items.ask: There were moments when I was on the blank of giving up.

items.s: ___ kept me going was the thought of the summer concert.
items.tip: What = the thing that: What kept me going was…
items.say: What kept me going was the thought of the summer concert.
items.ask: Blank kept me going was the thought of the summer concert.

items.s: When the night finally came, we played ___ though our lives depended on it.
items.tip: as though = as if (in a way that suggests).
items.say: When the night finally came, we played as though our lives depended on it.
items.ask: When the night finally came, we played blank though our lives depended on it.

items.s: The applause went ___ for what felt like an eternity.
items.tip: go on = continue.
items.say: The applause went on for what felt like an eternity.
items.ask: The applause went blank for what felt like an eternity.

items.s: I wouldn't change a single moment of it, ___ would anyone else in the orchestra.
items.tip: …, nor would anyone else = and also no one else would (question order after nor).
items.say: I wouldn't change a single moment of it, nor would anyone else in the orchestra.
items.ask: I wouldn't change a single moment of it, blank would anyone else in the orchestra.
